fields.hero_prompt: Build a freelancer landing page that saves every signup to a database I own.

faq_plan.q: What is a freelancer landing page?
How do I create a freelancer landing page?

plan.angle: Searchers for freelancer landing page want a page that turns a visitor into client work, and the ranking results are template galleries that stop at the design. This page follows the inquiry instead: four freelancers whose single page sells a service and lands every brief, rush request, instant quote and booked call in a table they own. It stays off sibling ground: no work galleries (portfolio), no about-me pages (personal), no link menus (link in bio), no job applications (resume). The FAQ covers the definition, building one, what to include, page versus full website, showing rates, brief form questions, link in bio use, length, testimonials and how it differs from a portfolio.
tab_stories: Copywriter Brona Marwood sells three packages on one page, and the brief form under each asks for the deadline, the budget and a link, so an email sequence brief arrives with its $1,400 budget and 3-week deadline already answered.

Video editor Caspar Askew asks every request for its turnaround, and anything under 72 hours is flagged as rush and sent to his Slack, so a 48-hour launch teaser outranks the 6-day and 10-day requests.
Translator Berit Kallio's page takes the file itself, reads the word count and multiplies it by her $0.12 rate, so a 4,800-word manual shows a $576 quote before she has opened the email.
Bookkeeper Lenore Sabel offers one next step, a 20-minute intro call, and her dashboard counts October as it runs: 22 inquiries, 9 booked calls, the latest from Cedar Spoon Diner.
